transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

I cannot tell you which part to buy yet because 'not draining' has several causes even after cleaning the filter. The most common next possibilities are a blockage further down the drain hose, something jammed in the pump impeller, or a failed pump motor. To separate these, please run a Drain or Spin cycle and listen at the bottom front of the machine while it tries to empty. Does the pump make a humming/buzzing noise (meaning it's trying but blocked), or is it completely silent (suggesting an electrical fault in the pump)?
It hums but the water doesn't go anywhere. Loud hum with a little rattle. No burning smell.

A loud hum with a rattle usually means the pump motor is working but something—like a coin, button, or hair grip—is jammed in the impeller blades. To confirm this, please switch the machine off and unplug it. Tell me if it spins freely or if you feel resistance/jamming.
Filter's already out and the impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. Also E18 shows on the display when it stalls.

This is most often caused by a foreign object like a coin, button, or hair grip caught in the impeller blades. To confirm this and see if you can clear it yourself, please reach inside the pump housing (past where the filter was) and feel if there is a specific hard object blocking the vanes, or does it just feel generally gritty? If you find an object, remove it carefully; if it's just gritty but no object is found, the impeller itself may be damaged or the pump motor failing.
It just feels gritty and stiff in places, I can't feel any coin or hard object. I'm not taking it apart any further, I haven't got the tools for the sump. So is it the pump I need?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. Yes, the symptoms point to a faulty drain pump. Since you do not have the tools to remove the sump housing for a full inspection or replacement, this requires an engineer to fit the new part safely.
